column1: # The builds bakeoff.sh reads with, cheapest first. `set` picks them: --build fitted (the default) runs the
# builds ocr-lab-setup found to fit (OCR-MODELS-2026-10-04.tsv); ocr-bakeoff-bits adds rows with its own set.
# chandra-ocr-2's fitted build is oQ8, because its GGUF Q4_K_M weights were deleted after ocr-lab-setup.
# repo `local/<name>` is a build converted here by convert-mlx.py into $OCRLAB/mlx/<name> (ocr-lab-round2:
# LightOnOCR's ocr-soup and base have no MLX build on the Hub). Their need_gb is 8: at 1540 px they peak near 11 GB,
# and base's first crops read, waiting for only 5, tripped the swap limit (OCR-MODELS-2026-10-05.tsv).
# read-mlx.py Churro's system prompt, repetition penalty and XML-to-text step (ocr-lab-round2, lab2-churro); the raw XML stays beside each
# qwen3-vl-8b-4bit and olmocr-2-7b-4bit (lab2-olmocr-qwen3vl) peak near 8 GB, hence need_gb 8; olmOCR 2's first read
# waiting for only 6 tripped the swap limit. Qwen3-VL-8B's weights are shared with Archive Suite's segbench in the same cache.
# qwen3.5-9b-4bit is `dropped` (owner, 2026-10-07, after 8 of 56 pages with weak reads): no run reads it, and
# ocr-bakeoff-score must skip it; its 8 readings stay on disk. While it was `owed`, bakeoff.sh gave it a last guarded try first.
# need_gb is the reclaimable memory the guard waits for before each read, higher for the larger builds, so a
# trip is less likely to measure the machine instead of the model. prompt `-` means read-mlx.py's default; `""` an empty prompt (LightOnOCR takes none). extra is passed to read-mlx.py.
# paddleocr-vl-1.6-4bit fits only as a region reader (lab3-paddle): a whole newspaper page or a truth crop passes its ~1 MP input
# cap and it reads 0.12-0.20 of the words; on DocLayout-YOLO regions it read 0.852. Its set is `fitted-regions`, not `fitted`, so
# `--build fitted` (whole pages and truth crops) does not score the cap as the model; ocr-hybrid-proto gives it regions.
# nara-qwen-3.5-2b-4bit (lab3-extras) reads with its own prompt.txt, copied into its build directory, which --prompt-file finds there.
# Set `bits` (ocr-bakeoff-bits): the top three's other build. Falcon-OCR-8bit is convert-mlx.py's -q --q-bits 8 then
# falcon-w13.py (without it every converted Falcon build reads noise). Falcon-OCR at 4 bits is `failed`: g64, g32, and 4 bits
# with embeddings, head and projector at 8 all read 0.000 of s01 and s03 and loop, so no run reads it. chandra-ocr-2-oQ4 is the
# same quantizer as the fitted oQ8, mostly 4-bit with some layers at 5-6. lightonocr-2-1b-4bit-1540-quiet is the fitted 4-bit
# read again, the same row under a new label: its first readings were timed on the busy night (ocr-bakeoff-score).
